docs.title: What is searchSDK?
docs.description: searchSDK is an open-source SDK that gives AI apps and agents one interface to many web search APIs.
docs.body:
searchSDK is an open-source, MIT-licensed SDK by Belweave. Your server makes one call; searchSDK sends it to the web search provider you name.

## What is a web search API for AI agents?

A web search API takes a query and returns results as data: URLs, titles, dates and excerpts. Agents use it to ground answers in current pages. Each provider has its own index, options, result fields, prices and limits.

## What does searchSDK do?

- Two calls, `search` and `contents`, with one result shape for every provider.
- Switch providers by changing one id.
- Fall back to other providers, in your order, only when you turn it on.
- Report a cost on every response and attempt, and where it came from.

## Which providers does it support?

Brave Search, Context.dev, Exa, Firecrawl, Perplexity, Tavily and TinyFish. Firecrawl is conformance-verified live in TypeScript and Python; Exa, Context.dev and TinyFish are live-tested in the 404-query benchmark; Brave Search, Perplexity and Tavily remain fixture-tested. [Each provider's page](https://searchsdk.dev/providers) lists what it supports.

## Which languages does it support?

TypeScript on Node 24 and Python 3.10 or newer, neither with runtime dependencies. TypeScript installs from npm as `@searchsdk/sdk` ([the quickstart](https://searchsdk.dev/docs)); Python is not on PyPI yet.

## Where do calls go?

From your server to the provider, with your key. No searchSDK service sits in between.

## How are providers compared?

An [open benchmark](https://searchsdk.dev/docs/benchmarks-method) ranks quality first, then reliability. The first live results (404 queries across three passes) are on [the benchmarks page](https://searchsdk.dev/benchmarks).

docs.title: searchSDK vs calling providers directly
docs.description: When to call a web search provider directly, and when searchSDK fits.
docs.body:
Calling a provider directly means using its own API or SDK. searchSDK is one interface over many. Both call the provider from your server; the difference is what you write and maintain.

| | Provider API or SDK | searchSDK |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shape | The provider's own | One for every provider, its body in `raw` |
| Switching | Rewrite the calls | Change the `provider` id |
| Fallback | You write it | Opt-in, in your order, every attempt recorded |
| Cost | From the provider's billing | On every response and attempt, with its source |
| Features | All of them, as they ship | The options each [provider's spec](https://searchsdk.dev/providers) maps |
| Status | Maintained by the provider | TypeScript on npm, Python from source; not verified against live APIs yet |

## When should you call a provider directly?

- You use one provider and do not plan to change.
- You need an option searchSDK does not map yet.
- You want a published package the provider supports.

## When does searchSDK fit?

- You call more than one provider, or want to try several with the same code.
- You want fallback when a provider is down, rate limited or out of quota.
- You want to know what each attempt cost, retries included.

## Can you use both?

Yes. `raw` keeps the provider's response and `providerOptions` passes options only one provider understands. A provider's own SDK can sit beside searchSDK in one app.

docs.title: Alternatives to searchSDK
docs.description: Other ways to give apps and agents web search, and when each one fits.
docs.body:
searchSDK is one way to give an app or agent web search across providers. These are the others.

## One provider's API or SDK

The plainest option when one provider covers your needs. You get every feature as it ships, in the provider's own shape. [The comparison](https://searchsdk.dev/docs/vs-provider-apis) covers the trade-offs.

## Your own adapter layer

Full control. You map each provider's options, fields, errors and prices yourself, and keep them current as the APIs change.

## Search tools in an agent framework

Frameworks such as LangChain and LlamaIndex include integrations for individual search providers. Each wraps one provider, so moving between providers means changing tools.

## A provider's MCP server

Several search providers publish MCP servers that let an agent call their API as a tool. Each server speaks for one provider.

## Hosted aggregators

Hosted services put several providers behind one API of their own, so your queries pass through them. With searchSDK, calls go from your server to the provider, with your key.

## How to compare them

- Which providers each covers, and which of their options.
- Whether cost is reported per attempt, retries and fallback included.
- Whether fallback is explicit and recorded.
- Where keys live, and which servers see your queries.
- The license, and whether the code is open.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.description: Short answers on searchSDK: providers, fallback, cost, benchmarks, status and license.
docs.body:
## What is searchSDK?

An open-source SDK by Belweave that gives AI apps and agents one interface to many web search APIs. Your server calls `search` or `contents`; searchSDK calls the provider you name.

## Which providers does it support?

Brave Search, Context.dev, Exa, Firecrawl, Perplexity, Tavily and TinyFish. [Their pages](https://searchsdk.dev/providers) list options, prices and limits.

## How does fallback work?

Off unless you set it. A call whose provider times out, is down, rate limited, out of quota or cannot honour an option then tries the next provider in your list. Every attempt is recorded.

## How is cost reported?

Every response and attempt carries a cost and its source: reported by the provider, computed from the list price, or unknown. An unknown price is `null`, never 0.

## How does the benchmark work?

Every provider gets the same queries. Known-answer tasks rank dependable providers; latency and cost never change rank. The 404-query run is on [Benchmarks](https://searchsdk.dev/benchmarks); judged scores wait for 100 human labels. [Method](https://searchsdk.dev/docs/benchmarks-method).

## How is it different from calling a provider directly?

One result shape, one id to change, explicit fallback and per-attempt cost. A direct call gets every provider feature first. [The comparison](https://searchsdk.dev/docs/vs-provider-apis).

## Is it on npm or PyPI?

TypeScript is on npm as [`@searchsdk/sdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@searchsdk/sdk). Python installs from source ([README](https://github.com/Belweave/searchSDK/tree/main/sdk/python)). Firecrawl is conformance-verified live; four providers are live-tested.

## What license is it under?

MIT. [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/Belweave/searchSDK).

docs.title: Privacy
docs.description: How the searchSDK website counts visits without cookies, and why the SDK itself sends nothing.
docs.body:
## The SDK

The SDK has no analytics and no telemetry. A call goes from your server to the provider you name, with your key, and nowhere else. Nothing reaches Belweave or this site.

## This website

The site counts visits with PostHog in cookieless mode: no cookies, no local or session storage, no consent banner. PostHog derives a visitor hash on its servers that changes every day, so a visit cannot be linked to the next day's.

It measures:

- pages viewed and left, and page load timings (Core Web Vitals);
- clicks on links and buttons, the destination host of links to other sites, and which code blocks are copied;
- the length of a docs search, never its text;
- fetches of `llms.txt`, the Markdown copies, the sitemap and `robots.txt`: the path, the kind of client (a named crawler or agent, a browser or a tool), the referring host and the country.

It never records what you type, session replays, names or accounts, or a URL's query string. PostHog is set to discard IP addresses.

A browser that sends Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control loads no analytics.

Events go to `/ingest` on this site, which forwards them to PostHog's US cloud.

## Package statistics

Once a day the site records public figures: npm download counts, and the GitHub repository's stars, forks, watchers and release downloads.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.description: Install searchSDK from npm, set a provider key and run your first web search from TypeScript.
docs.body:
searchSDK gives AI apps and agents one interface to many web search APIs. This page installs it and runs a first search.

## Install

```sh
npm install @searchsdk/sdk
```

It has no runtime dependencies and needs a standard `fetch`. Tested on Node 24.

## Add a key

Each provider reads its documented variable, such as `EXA_API_KEY`. Keys stay on your server and are never logged.

```sh
export EXA_API_KEY="your-key"
```

## Search

```ts
import { search } from "@searchsdk/sdk";

const { results, cost } = await search("vector database indexing", { provider: "exa", maxResults: 5 });
for (const r of results) console.log(r.title, r.url);
console.log(cost.usd, cost.source);
```

## Fall back

A client can try other providers, in order, when one is unavailable, rate limited, out of quota or cannot honour an option. Fallback and retries are off unless you set them.

```ts
import { createClient } from "@searchsdk/sdk";

const client = createClient({ provider: "exa", fallback: ["tavily"], maxRetries: 1 });
const res = await client.search("vector database indexing");
console.log(res.provider, res.attempts.length);
```

## Next

- [Search](https://searchsdk.dev/docs/search): options, results and errors.
- [Contents](https://searchsdk.dev/docs/contents): the text of pages.
- [Providers](https://searchsdk.dev/docs/providers): ids, keys and provider options.
- [Cost](https://searchsdk.dev/docs/cost): what each call cost.

docs.title: Search
docs.description: Search the web through one provider or a fallback chain, with filters, deadlines, retries and a cancel signal.
docs.body:
`search(query, options)` uses keys from the environment. `createClient(config).search(query, options)` takes keys and defaults once.

```ts
import { search } from "@searchsdk/sdk";

const controller = new AbortController();
const res = await search("postgres full text search", {
  provider: "tavily",
  maxResults: 5,
  recency: "month",
  country: "DE",
  timeoutMs: 10_000,
  signal: controller.signal,
});
```

## Options

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `provider` | Provider id; required unless the client sets one |
| `fallback` | Providers to try next, in order |
| `maxResults` | 1 to 100; default 10 |
| `includeDomains`, `excludeDomains` | Domain filters |
| `recency` | `day`, `week`, `month` or `year` |
| `startDate`, `endDate` | Inclusive `YYYY-MM-DD`, by publication date |
| `country`, `language` | ISO 3166-1 and ISO 639-1 codes |
| `depth` | `fast`, `standard` or `deep` |
| `providerOptions` | Options one provider understands, keyed by id |
| `timeoutMs` | Deadline for the whole call; default 30 s |
| `attemptTimeoutMs` | Deadline for each attempt |
| `maxRetries` | Retries of transient failures; default 0 |
| `maxResponseBytes` | Largest response read |
| `signal` | Cancels the call |

An option a provider cannot honour fails as `unsupported` before anything is sent. [Each provider's page](https://searchsdk.dev/providers) lists what it honours.

## Results

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `url` | Page address |
| `title`, `author`, `publishedAt` | Or `null` when the provider has none |
| `excerpts` | Text the provider matched |
| `rank` | Position, from 1 |
| `providerFields` | Provider-scoped values such as scores; not comparable across providers |

The response also carries `provider`, `cost`, `requestId`, `latencyMs`, `warnings`, `attempts` and `raw`, the provider's own body.

## Errors

Failures throw `SearchError` with a fixed `code` and the `attempts` made.

```ts
import { search, SearchError } from "@searchsdk/sdk";

try {
  await search("postgres full text search", { provider: "brave", includeDomains: ["postgresql.org"] });
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof SearchError) console.log(e.code, e.field, e.attempts);
}
```

docs.title: Providers
docs.description: How searchSDK names providers, finds their keys, passes provider-only options and keeps raw responses.
docs.body:
A provider is a search API that searchSDK calls from your server. [Each provider's page](https://searchsdk.dev/providers) shows what it supports, its prices and limits, read from the registry.

## Ids and keys

| Provider | Id | Key variable | Calls |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Brave Search](https://searchsdk.dev/providers/brave) | `brave` | `BRAVE_API_KEY` | search |
| [Context.dev](https://searchsdk.dev/providers/context) | `context` | `CONTEXT_DEV_API_KEY` | search, contents |
| [Exa](https://searchsdk.dev/providers/exa) | `exa` | `EXA_API_KEY` | search, contents |
| [Firecrawl](https://searchsdk.dev/providers/firecrawl) | `firecrawl` | `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` | search, contents |
| [Perplexity](https://searchsdk.dev/providers/perplexity) | `perplexity` | `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY` | search, contents |
| [Tavily](https://searchsdk.dev/providers/tavily) | `tavily` | `TAVILY_API_KEY` | search, contents |
| [TinyFish](https://searchsdk.dev/providers/tinyfish) | `tinyfish` | `TINYFISH_API_KEY` | search, contents |

Ids are lowercase and typed as `ProviderId`. Keys come from each provider's documented variable, or from `keys`:

```ts
import { createClient } from "@searchsdk/sdk";

const client = createClient({
  provider: "brave",
  fallback: ["firecrawl"],
  keys: { brave: "your-brave-key", firecrawl: "your-firecrawl-key" },
});
```

Pass `env` instead to read variables from elsewhere, such as Worker bindings. A fallback without a key is skipped with a warning. Never ship a key to a browser or mobile app.

## Provider options

Options only one provider understands go under its id, typed per provider and checked before sending.

```ts
import { search } from "@searchsdk/sdk";

const res = await search("rust async runtimes", {
  provider: "exa",
  providerOptions: { exa: { category: "news" } },
});
```

## Raw responses

`raw` is the provider's own parsed body, and `providerFields` keeps fields with no common name.

```ts
import { search } from "@searchsdk/sdk";

const res = await search("rust async runtimes", { provider: "tavily" });
console.log(res.raw, res.results[0]?.providerFields);
```

## The registry

Provider behaviour is data, one spec per provider. `registry` exports it; `createClient({ registry })` accepts edited copies and validates them.

docs.title: Benchmarks method
docs.description: How searchSDK benchmarks web search providers end to end, scores answer quality and ranks the leaderboard.
docs.body:
Every provider runs the same queries through searchSDK, end to end, with settings tuned to suit it. The harness is open: anyone can rerun it with their own keys.

First live results (404 queries, three passes) are on [Benchmarks](https://searchsdk.dev/benchmarks); judged scores wait for 100 human labels.

## The run

- About 400 queries, once a month.
- Each query goes to every provider with the same deadline and result limit.
- Every response, failure and timing is recorded.

## Quality

- **Known-answer tasks** set the rank. Each query has a checked answer. A provider scores when its top results, or the pages behind them, contain it. The harness reads those pages itself, obeying robots.txt, so no provider fetches for its rivals. A page it cannot read counts the same for everyone.
- **Judged relevance** is a separate column. One model grades results against a published rubric. People check a sample, and the column appears only when they agree with it.

## Ranking

1. Providers with fewer than 95% usable responses are marked unreliable and ranked below every dependable one.
2. The known-answer score decides the rest.
3. Two providers are tied unless the gap is statistically clear and at least 6 points.

Latency and cost are reported beside the rank. Cost never changes rank.

## Funding

Runs are paid for by provider credits, donations and a capped monthly budget from the maintainer. Every source is disclosed with the results.

docs.title: MCP server
docs.description: Connect Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Codex and other agents to the free searchSDK docs MCP server, or run search locally.
docs.body:
The public server at `https://searchsdk.dev/mcp` is free and needs no key. It serves the docs and the provider registry only: it never calls a provider, holds no key, fetches no URL and runs no code. It speaks Streamable HTTP, stateless, on MCP revision 2026-07-28, and answers 2025 clients too.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `search_docs` | Full-text search over every docs section |
| `get_doc` | One docs page as Markdown |
| `list_providers` | Every provider, its key variable and verification status |
| `get_provider` | Options, limits, list prices, rate limits and sources |
| `estimate_cost` | `costBound` and `listPrice` for a call; nothing is sent |
| `validate_options` | Whether a provider can honour your options, checked by the SDK without sending |
| `get_example` | Typechecked TypeScript examples for a task |

Resources: every docs page, every provider spec, the shared policy and the [agent skill](https://searchsdk.dev/docs/agent-skill). Prompts: `integrate-searchsdk` and `choose-provider`.

## Add it

Claude Code:

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http searchsdk https://searchsdk.dev/mcp
```

Cursor (`.cursor/mcp.json`):

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "searchsdk": { "url": "https://searchsdk.dev/mcp" } } }
```

VS Code with Copilot and Claude Code projects (`.mcp.json` at the workspace root):

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "searchsdk": { "type": "http", "url": "https://searchsdk.dev/mcp" } } }
```

Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`):

```toml
[mcp_servers.searchsdk]
url = "https://searchsdk.dev/mcp"
```

Gemini CLI (`.gemini/settings.json`):

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "searchsdk": { "httpUrl": "https://searchsdk.dev/mcp" } } }
```

`/api/mcp` answers the same as `/mcp`.

## Run search locally

`@searchsdk/mcp` adds `search` and `contents` tools that run through `@searchsdk/sdk` on your machine, over stdio, with your own provider keys from its environment. Keys are never logged or returned. Source: [sdk/mcp](https://github.com/Belweave/searchSDK/tree/main/sdk/mcp).

```sh
claude mcp add --env EXA_API_KEY=your-key --transport stdio searchsdk-local -- npx -y @searchsdk/mcp
```

Optional variables: `SEARCHSDK_PROVIDER`, `SEARCHSDK_FALLBACK`, `SEARCHSDK_MAX_RETRIES`, `SEARCHSDK_TIMEOUT_MS` and `SEARCHSDK_MAX_CHARS`. Each `search` or `contents` call may be billed by the provider.

docs.body:
The skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md` and reference files, in the Agent Skills format. It teaches a coding agent to install searchSDK, choose a provider and fallback, keep keys on the server, read cost and warnings, handle errors and wrap search as a tool.

## Install in Claude Code

For every project (personal skills):

```sh
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cd ~/.claude/skills
curl -fsSLO https://searchsdk.dev/skills/searchsdk.zip && unzip -o searchsdk.zip && rm searchsdk.zip
```

For one repository, unzip it into `.claude/skills/` and commit it. Claude Code loads it when a task touches web search or searchSDK.

## Files

- [`SKILL.md`](https://searchsdk.dev/skills/searchsdk/SKILL.md): the instructions, also at [`/skill.md`](https://searchsdk.dev/skill.md).
- [`references/api.md`](https://searchsdk.dev/skills/searchsdk/references/api.md): options and response fields.
- [`references/errors.md`](https://searchsdk.dev/skills/searchsdk/references/errors.md): error and warning codes.
- [`references/agent-tools.md`](https://searchsdk.dev/skills/searchsdk/references/agent-tools.md): tool wrappers for agent frameworks.

Source: [`skills/searchsdk`](https://github.com/Belweave/searchSDK/tree/main/skills/searchsdk). Other agents that read Agent Skills take the same folder. The [MCP server](https://searchsdk.dev/docs/mcp) serves the skill as resources too.

docs.title: Options reference
docs.description: Every option of search, contents and createClient in searchSDK, with types, defaults and limits from the SDK source.
docs.body:
Every call option and client setting, read from the SDK's types and the shared policy. Unknown option names fail as `invalid_request`; an option a provider cannot honour fails as `unsupported` before anything is sent.

## search(query, options)

`query` is trimmed of blank characters and must keep 1 to 2000 code points, with no control, bidirectional-control or tag characters.

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maxResults?` | `number` | Results wanted: 1 to 100, default 10. More than a provider's limit is `unsupported` there; a provider without a count parameter is trimmed by searchSDK. |
| `includeDomains?` | `readonly string[]` | Only results from these hosts. Lowercased and de-duplicated; must not overlap `excludeDomains`. |
| `excludeDomains?` | `readonly string[]` | No results from these hosts. |
| `recency?` | `Recency` | `day`, `week`, `month` or `year` (day = 1 day, week = 7 days, month = 30 days, year = 365 days). Not with `startDate` or `endDate`. |
| `startDate?` | `string` | Inclusive `YYYY-MM-DD`, by publication date. |
| `endDate?` | `string` | Inclusive `YYYY-MM-DD`, by publication date; not before `startDate`. |
| `country?` | `string` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code; sent upper case. |
| `language?` | `string` | ISO 639-1 code; sent lower case. |
| `depth?` | `Depth` | `fast`, `standard` or `deep`, mapped to the provider's own levels; it can change the price tier. |
| `providerOptions?` | `SearchProviderOptions` | Options one provider understands, keyed by id, validated against its spec before sending. |

## Call options

Both `search` and `contents` take these.

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `provider?` | `ProviderId` | Provider id. Required unless the client sets `provider`. |
| `fallback?` | `readonly ProviderId[]` | Providers tried next, in order, after a fallback-eligible failure. Overrides the client's list. A provider is tried once. |
| `timeoutMs?` | `number` | Deadline for the whole call, retries and fallback included: 1 to 300000 ms, default 30000. |
| `attemptTimeoutMs?` | `number` | Deadline for each attempt: 1 to 300000 ms, default `timeoutMs`. An attempt that passes it fails as `attempt_timeout`. |
| `maxRetries?` | `number` | Retries of a transient failure on the same provider: 0 to 5, default 0. |
| `maxResponseBytes?` | `number` | Largest response body read: 1 KiB to 100 MiB; default 10 MiB for search, 50 MiB for contents. |
| `signal?` | `AbortSignal` | An `AbortSignal`; aborting fails the call as `aborted`. |

## contents(urls, options)

`urls` is one URL or a list of 1 to 100, each at most 2048 characters, http or https. Each provider takes fewer per call; see [Provider support](https://searchsdk.dev/docs/reference/provider-support).

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `providerOptions?` | `ContentsProviderOptions` | Options one provider understands, keyed by id, validated against its spec before sending. |

## createClient(config)

A client checks its settings when it is created. Call options override client settings.

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `provider?` | `ProviderId` | Default provider for calls that name none. |
| `fallback?` | `readonly ProviderId[]` | Default fallback chain. |
| `keys?` | `Partial<Record<ProviderId, string>>` | API keys by provider id. A missing key is read from the provider's documented variables. |
| `env?` | `Readonly<Record<string, string \| undefined>>` | Variables to read keys from instead of `process.env`, such as Worker bindings. |
| `timeoutMs?` | `number` | Default call deadline (see call options). |
| `attemptTimeoutMs?` | `number` | Default attempt deadline. |
| `maxRetries?` | `number` | Default retries. |
| `maxResponseBytes?` | `number` | Default response size limit. |
| `fetch?` | `typeof globalThis.fetch` | The `fetch` to use. Tests inject one; the default is the platform's. |
| `clock?` | `Clock` | Time source (`now`, `setTimeout`, `clearTimeout`); tests inject a virtual clock. |
| `random?` | `() => number` | Uniform source in [0, 1) for retry jitter. Backoff starts at 250 ms and is capped at 5000 ms; a `Retry-After` over 60000 ms is not waited for. |
| `diagnostics?` | `(event: AttemptDiagnostics<ProviderId>) => void` | Opt-in hook called once per sent attempt with the redacted request, status, headers, bounded body and how the spec's paths resolved. Keys never appear; what it throws is ignored. |
| `registry?` | `Readonly<Record<ProviderId, unknown>>` | Provider specs to use instead of the built-in registry, keyed by id. Validated and copied; their keys become the accepted ids. |

docs.title: Responses reference
docs.description: Every field of searchSDK search and contents responses: results, pages, cost, attempts, warnings and cost bounds.
docs.body:
Every response field, read from the SDK's types. Both responses share the common fields.

## Common fields

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | `ProviderId` | The provider that answered (a fallback, when `fallback_used` is in `warnings`). |
| `cost` | `Cost` | What the successful attempt cost (see Cost). |
| `requestId` | `string \| null` | The provider's request id, or `null`. |
| `latencyMs` | `number` | Milliseconds from the start of the call to the answer. |
| `warnings` | `Warning<ProviderId>[]` | Non-fatal notes (see Warnings). |
| `attempts` | `Attempt<ProviderId>[]` | Every attempt, skipped ones included, in order. |
| `raw` | `unknown` | The provider's parsed JSON body. |

## SearchResponse

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `results` | `SearchResult[]` | Normalized results; `[]` is a success. |

### SearchResult

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | `string` | The result's address. |
| `title` | `string \| null` | Title, or `null`. |
| `excerpts` | `string[]` | Text the provider matched; the kind (description, content chunks, highlights) is on each provider's page. |
| `publishedAt` | `string \| null` | Publication time as an ISO 8601 string, or `null`. |
| `author` | `string \| null` | Author, or `null`. |
| `rank` | `number` | Position, from 1. |
| `providerFields` | `Record<string, unknown>` | Provider-scoped values such as scores and ids. Not comparable across providers. |

## ContentsResponse

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pages` | `Page[]` | One page per requested URL, in order. |

### Page

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | `string` | The URL as requested. |
| `status` | `"ok" \| "failed"` | `ok` or `failed`. One failed page never fails the call. |

| `author` | `string \| null` | Author, or `null`. |
| `error` | `{ code: string \| null; message: string \| null } \| null` | For a failed page: the provider's code and message (`missing` when the provider returned nothing for the URL). |

## Cost

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `usd` | `number \| null` | USD, or `null` when the price is not known. Never 0 for unknown. |
| `estimated` | `boolean` | False only for an exact provider-reported figure, or when nothing was sent. |
| `source` | `CostSource` | `reported`, `reported-credits`, `computed`, `unknown` or `none`. |
| `credits?` | `number` | Credits the provider reported, for credit pricing. |

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | `ProviderId` | Provider tried. |
| `outcome` | `"ok" \| "error" \| "skipped"` | `ok`, `error` or `skipped` (no key, or an option the provider cannot honour). |
| `code?` | `ErrorCode` | Error code of a failed or skipped attempt. |
| `status?` | `number` | HTTP status, when one arrived. |
| `startMs` | `number` | Milliseconds from the start of the call. |
| `durationMs` | `number` | How long the attempt took. |
| `retryAfterMs?` | `number` | The provider's `Retry-After`, in milliseconds. |
| `billed` | `Billed` | `yes` (a 2xx), `possible` (sent, no answer) or `no` (not sent, or an error status). |
| `cost` | `Cost` | This attempt's own cost; for `possible`, what it costs if it was billed. |

| `code` | `string` | Warning code (see Warnings). |
| `provider` | `ProviderId` | Provider it concerns. |
| `message?` | `string` | The provider's message, when it sent one. |

Returned by `costBound(spec, kind, input)`. `listPrice(spec, kind, { count })` returns a `Cost`.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `usd` | `number \| null` | The most one request can cost at the highest documented rate, or `null` when it cannot be bounded. |

docs.title: Error codes reference
docs.description: Every searchSDK SearchError code: what it means, whether it is retried, falls back or may be billed, and what to do.
docs.body:
Every failure throws `SearchError` with one fixed `code`. Messages are fixed per code and never include keys or response bodies. Retries need `maxRetries`; fallback needs `fallback`.

## Codes

| Code | HTTP status | Retried | Falls back | Meaning and what to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid_request` | – | no | no | Fix the input: `field` names the option or `query`. Nothing was sent. |
| `configuration` | – | no | no | Fix the client: a missing or unusable key (`field: "keys"`), no or an unknown provider, or a bad setting. |
| `unsupported` | – | no | yes | The provider cannot express this request (`field` says which option). A fallback skips it; otherwise drop the option or pick another provider. |
| `auth` | 401 | no | no | The provider rejected the key. Check the key variable. |
| `forbidden` | 403 | no | no | The key is valid but not allowed this call (plan or permission). |
| `quota` | 402 | no | yes | Out of credits or over a plan limit. Top up, or fall back. |
| `rate_limit` | 429 | yes | yes | Too many requests. Set `maxRetries` to honour `Retry-After`, or fall back. |
| `unavailable` | 408, other 500–599 | yes | yes | A 5xx or 408. Retry, or fall back. |
| `provider_error` | other 400–499 | no | no | Any other 4xx: the provider refused the request as sent. `providerCode` and the attempt status help. |
| `network` | – | yes | yes | No answer: the connection failed or broke off. It may have been billed. |
| `attempt_timeout` | – | yes | yes | One attempt passed `attemptTimeoutMs`. Retried and falls back. |
| `timeout` | – | no | no | The whole call passed `timeoutMs`. Raise it or lower retries. |
| `aborted` | – | no | no | Your `signal` aborted the call. |
| `invalid_response` | – | no | no | A 2xx that is not a UTF-8 JSON object, or a status searchSDK cannot map (3xx). Billed for a 2xx, never retried. |
| `spec_mismatch` | – | no | no | A 2xx JSON object without the list the spec reads; `path` names it and `raw` keeps the body. Our spec and the provider disagree: report it. |
| `response_too_large` | – | no | no | A 2xx over `maxResponseBytes`. Raise the limit or ask for fewer items. |

An attempt that got a 2xx is billed, so it is never retried; one that got an error status is not billed. With no status, `network`, `attempt_timeout`, `timeout` and `aborted` attempts are billed `possible`, and the rest were never sent. An empty result list is a success, never an error.

## Provider status rules

Some providers signal a code with their own status or body. These rules run before the shared status table.

| Provider | Status | When | Code |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Brave Search | 429 | error.code = "QUOTA_LIMITED" | `quota` |
| Perplexity | 401 | error.type = "insufficient_quota" | `quota` |
| Tavily | 432 | – | `quota` |
| Tavily | 433 | – | `quota` |
| Tavily | 434 | – | `unavailable` |
| TinyFish | 429 | error.details.reason = "free_allowance_exhausted" | `quota` |

## SearchError fields

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | `ErrorCode` | One of the codes above. |
| `provider?` | `AnyProviderId` | The provider of the failing attempt. |
| `status?` | `number` | HTTP status, when one arrived. |
| `providerCode?` | `string` | The provider's own machine-readable code, when its spec says where to read it. |
| `retryAfterMs?` | `number` | The provider's `Retry-After`, in milliseconds. |
| `field?` | `string` | The option that failed validation or that the provider cannot honour. |
| `path?` | `string` | For `spec_mismatch`: the spec path the body did not have. |
| `attempts` | `Attempt<AnyProviderId>[]` | Every attempt made before the failure, with its cost and billing. |
| `raw?` | `unknown` | The parsed body of a 2xx that could not be mapped. |

`message` is the fixed text for the code. Guides: [Errors and troubleshooting](https://searchsdk.dev/docs/guides/errors).

docs.description: Every warning code searchSDK or a provider spec can add to a response, what it means and which providers send it.
docs.body:
`warnings` holds notes that do not fail the call. Each has a `code`, the `provider`, and a `message` or `count` when there is one.

## From searchSDK

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `fallback_key_missing` | A fallback provider has no key and will be skipped. |
| `fallback_used` | The answer came from a fallback, not the first provider. |
| `invalid_rows_dropped` | Results or pages without a URL were dropped; `count` says how many. |
| `unmatched_pages` | The provider returned pages that match no requested URL (by URL key); `count` says how many. |

## From provider responses

The registry maps these from a provider's own body.

| Code | Meaning | Sent by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `partial_results` | The provider says its answer is partial. | Context.dev search, Context.dev contents |
| `provider_notice` | The provider's own notice, with its `message`. | Exa search |
| `provider_warning` | The provider's own warning, with its `message`. | Exa search, Firecrawl search, Firecrawl contents |

Check warnings after every call: `fallback_used` means another provider answered, and its prices and fields differ.

docs.description: Releases of the searchSDK TypeScript package, the MCP server and the documentation, newest first.
docs.body:
## 2026-11-25

- `@searchsdk/sdk` 0.1.1: the first correct build. 0.1.0 was packed from a stale build that lacked the `spec_mismatch` error and rejected the current registry; it is deprecated. No API changed.
- `@searchsdk/mcp` 0.1.0 on npm: a local MCP server over stdio with the docs and registry tools plus `search` and `contents` through your own keys (`npx -y @searchsdk/mcp`).
- A public docs MCP server at `https://searchsdk.dev/mcp`, on MCP revision 2026-07-28.
- An [agent skill](https://searchsdk.dev/docs/agent-skill), guides for fallback, budgets, agent tools, errors and migration, and reference pages generated from the SDK source and the registry.
- Docs pages can be copied as Markdown or opened in an AI assistant.

## @searchsdk/sdk 0.1.0 (2026-11-25)

First release, on npm as `@searchsdk/sdk`. No provider is verified against its live API yet: every spec is written from public docs and tested against synthetic fixtures.

- `search` and `contents` over a shared, declarative provider registry: Brave Search, Context.dev, Exa, Firecrawl, Perplexity, Tavily and TinyFish. Brave has search only.
- Per-attempt cost: reported, computed from list prices, or unknown (never $0 for unknown), and whether each attempt was billed. `costBound` and `listPrice` price a call before it is sent.
- Retries (off by default), `Retry-After`, per-attempt and per-call deadlines, cancellation, response size limits and explicit fallback.
- Fixed error codes on `SearchError`, including `spec_mismatch` with the failing path, and an opt-in diagnostics hook.

The Python runtime in `sdk/python` is not on PyPI yet.

# searchSDK API reference (condensed)

Generated pages with every field: https://searchsdk.dev/docs/reference/options and https://searchsdk.dev/docs/reference/responses.

## Exports

`search`, `contents`, `createClient`, `costBound`, `listPrice`, `registry`, `policy`, `urlKey`, `SearchError`, and the types (`ProviderId`, `SearchOptions`, `SearchResponse`, `ContentsResponse`, `Attempt`, `Cost`, ...).

## search options

| Option | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `provider` | Required unless the client sets one |
| `fallback` | Providers tried next, in order; `[]` turns the client's list off for one call |
| `maxResults` | 1 to 100, default 10; above a provider's limit is `unsupported` there |
| `includeDomains`, `excludeDomains` | Hostnames; must not overlap |
| `recency` | `day`, `week`, `month`, `year`; not with dates |
| `startDate`, `endDate` | Inclusive `YYYY-MM-DD`, by publication date |
| `country`, `language` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, ISO 639-1 |
| `depth` | `fast`, `standard`, `deep`; may change the price tier |
| `providerOptions` | `{ <id>: { ... } }`, validated per provider |
| `timeoutMs` | Whole call, default 30000, max 300000 |
| `attemptTimeoutMs` | Each attempt, default `timeoutMs` |
| `maxRetries` | 0 to 5, default 0 |
| `maxResponseBytes` | Default 10 MiB for search, 50 MiB for contents |
| `signal` | `AbortSignal` |

`contents(urls, options)` takes the call options (`provider`, `fallback`, `providerOptions`, timeouts, `maxRetries`, `maxResponseBytes`, `signal`) and 1 to 100 http(s) URLs; each provider allows fewer per call.

## Client settings

`createClient({ provider, fallback, keys, env, timeoutMs, attemptTimeoutMs, maxRetries, maxResponseBytes, fetch, diagnostics, registry })`. Settings are checked when the client is created.

## Responses

Common: `provider`, `cost`, `requestId`, `latencyMs`, `warnings`, `attempts`, `raw`. Search adds `results`; contents adds `pages`.

- Result: `url`, `title | null`, `excerpts: string[]`, `publishedAt | null`, `author | null`, `rank` (from 1), `providerFields`.
- Page: `url`, `status`, `finalUrl`, `title`, `content`, `publishedAt`, `author`, `error: { code, message } | null` (`missing` when the provider returned nothing for the URL).
- Cost: `usd | null`, `estimated`, `source` (`reported`, `reported-credits`, `computed`, `unknown`, `none`), `credits?`.
- Attempt: `provider`, `outcome` (`ok`, `error`, `skipped`), `code?`, `status?`, `startMs`, `durationMs`, `retryAfterMs?`, `billed`, `cost`.

## Budget sketch

```ts
import { costBound, registry, type ProviderId } from "@searchsdk/sdk";

const chain: ProviderId[] = ["exa", "tavily"];
let reserve = 0;
for (const id of chain) {
  const bound = costBound(registry[id], "search", { maxResults: 10 });
  if (bound.usd === null) throw new Error(`${id}: ${bound.unknownBecause}`);
  reserve += bound.usd;
}
console.log(reserve);
```

# searchSDK

searchSDK (always written exactly so) is an MIT-licensed TypeScript SDK by Belweave. Two calls, `search` and `contents`, one result shape for every provider. Zero runtime dependencies; needs standard `fetch`; tested on Node 24. Docs: https://searchsdk.dev/docs (every page has a `.md` copy, and https://searchsdk.dev/llms-full.txt has them all).

Firecrawl (`search` and `contents`) is conformance-verified against its live API in TypeScript and Python; Exa, Context.dev, TinyFish and Firecrawl have been tested live across smoke, tuning and 4,848 benchmark search calls. Brave Search, Perplexity and Tavily remain fixture-tested. Published 404-query known-answer benchmark results are at https://searchsdk.dev/benchmarks (judged relevance withheld pending 100 human labels); do not make unmeasured claims about unrun providers.

## Install

```sh
npm install @searchsdk/sdk
```

The Python runtime (`sdk/python` in the repository) is not on PyPI.

## Keys

Each provider reads its documented variable: `EXA_API_KEY`, `TAVILY_API_KEY`, `BRAVE_API_KEY`, `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY`, `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`, `CONTEXT_DEV_API_KEY`, `TINYFISH_API_KEY`. Or pass `createClient({ keys: { exa: "..." } })`, or `env` for Worker bindings.

- Server only. Never put a key in browser, mobile or edge-client code; app code calls your own backend.
- A missing primary key throws `configuration` (`field: "keys"`) before anything is sent; a fallback without a key is skipped with a `fallback_key_missing` warning.

## search vs contents

- `search(query, options)`: ranked results (`url`, `title`, `excerpts`, `publishedAt`, `author`, `rank`, `providerFields`).
- `contents(urls, options)`: page text, one `page` per requested URL in order, `status: "ok" | "failed"`. A failed page does not fail the call.
- Brave Search has no contents endpoint. URLs per contents call differ by provider (Context.dev and Firecrawl take 1).

```ts
import { createClient } from "@searchsdk/sdk";

const client = createClient({ provider: "exa", fallback: ["tavily"], maxRetries: 1 });
const res = await client.search("sqlite wal mode", { maxResults: 5, recency: "year" });
const pages = await client.contents(res.results.slice(0, 3).map((r) => r.url));
for (const p of pages.pages) console.log(p.status, p.url, p.content?.length ?? p.error?.code);
```

## Choosing a provider and fallback

- `provider` is required on a call unless the client sets one. Ids: `brave`, `context`, `exa`, `firecrawl`, `perplexity`, `tavily`, `tinyfish`.
- Check support before writing options: an option a provider cannot honour fails as `unsupported` before sending (for example `startDate` on Brave, `maxResults` above a provider's limit). The MCP tool `validate_options` or https://searchsdk.dev/docs/reference/provider-support shows the matrix.
- Retries and fallback are off by default. Set `maxRetries` (0 to 5) and `fallback: [...]`.
- Retried: `network`, `rate_limit`, `unavailable`, `attempt_timeout`. Falls back on those plus `quota` and `unsupported`. `auth`, `forbidden`, `provider_error`, `invalid_response`, `spec_mismatch`, `response_too_large`, `timeout` and `aborted` stop the call.
- Provider-only options go under `providerOptions: { <id>: {...} }`; each provider in a chain gets only its own.

## Cost, attempts and warnings

Read these on every response; they are the point of the SDK.

- `res.cost`: `{ usd, estimated, source }`. `usd` is `null` when the price is unknown. Never treat `null` as 0.
- `res.attempts`: every attempt, including skipped ones, each with `billed` (`yes`, `possible`, `no`) and its own `cost`. Sum attempts with `billed !== "no"` for spend; a `SearchError` carries `attempts` too.
- `res.warnings`: `fallback_used` (another provider answered: check `res.provider`), `invalid_rows_dropped`, `unmatched_pages`, `partial_results`, `provider_warning`, `provider_notice`.
- Before a call, `costBound(registry.exa, "search", { maxResults: 10 })` gives the most it can cost; `null` with `unknownBecause` when it cannot be bounded.

## Errors

Every failure is a `SearchError` with a fixed `code`; switch on `code`, never on `message`. `field` names the bad option, `status` the HTTP status, `retryAfterMs` the provider's `Retry-After`. An empty `results` array is a success, not an error. Full table: [references/errors.md](references/errors.md).

```ts
import { search, SearchError } from "@searchsdk/sdk";

try {
  await search("postgres vacuum", { provider: "brave", startDate: "2026-01-01" });
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof SearchError && e.code === "unsupported") console.log("Brave cannot filter by", e.field);
}
```

## As an agent tool

Return compact results (title, url, date, first excerpt) and return `{ error: e.code }` instead of throwing so the model can recover. Cap `maxResults`. Framework wrappers (Vercel AI SDK `tool()`, OpenAI Responses function calling, Anthropic tool use): [references/agent-tools.md](references/agent-tools.md).

## MCP server

- Public, free, keyless, docs and registry only: `claude mcp add --transport http searchsdk https://searchsdk.dev/mcp`. Tools: `search_docs`, `get_doc`, `list_providers`, `get_provider`, `estimate_cost`, `validate_options`, `get_example`. Use them to confirm an option or price before writing code.
- Local `@searchsdk/mcp` (stdio) adds real `search` and `contents` with the user's keys. Run it with `npx -y @searchsdk/mcp`.

## Pitfalls

- The npm name is `@searchsdk/sdk`, not `searchsdk` or `search-sdk`.
- Unknown option names throw `invalid_request`; do not pass provider-native names (`numResults`, `max_results`) at the top level.
- `recency` cannot be combined with `startDate` or `endDate`; dates are inclusive `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- `providerFields` (scores and ids) are not comparable across providers.
- `raw` is the provider's whole body; do not send it to a model unfiltered.
- The exported `registry` is frozen. Pass edited copies to `createClient({ registry })`.

More: [references/api.md](references/api.md) for every option and response field.
